title: Why do zebras have stripes?
examples: Do zebras use their stripes for anything?
Are the stripes just for looks?
Why do some animals have stripes?

explain.say: Some students wonder why zebras have black and white stripes.
One idea is that the stripes confuse things that try to eat them.
Another reason is that the stripes might help the zebra stay cool in the sun.
A concrete example is that stripes might confuse a lion's attack.
For a real-life example, think about a busy crowd of people.
A common mistake is thinking stripes only help hide in the grass.

items: It is not just about hiding

faq.q: Do all zebras have the same stripes?
faq.a: No, the exact pattern of stripes can be different on every zebra. This makes them even harder to spot.
asks: Are all zebra stripes the same?

faq.q: Do the stripes help them swim?
faq.a: The stripes are mainly thought to help them on land, not in the water. Their stripes are for confusing things nearby.
asks: Are stripes useful in the river?
Do stripes help when they swim?

faq.q: Are the stripes a warning sign?
faq.a: Some stripes can act like a warning, but for zebras, the main ideas are confusing predators or cooling down. It is more about trickery.
asks: Do the stripes warn others away?

faq.q: Do the stripes help them find food?
faq.a: No, the stripes are not really for finding food. They are more about keeping them safe from other animals.
asks: Is finding food related to stripes?

faq.q: Why are they black and white?
faq.a: The contrast between black and white is very strong. This contrast is very good at confusing the eyes of a predator.
asks: What makes the colors so clear?

facts: Zebra stripes are thought to confuse predators.
The stripes may also help the zebra to regulate its body temperature.
The pattern is unique to each individual zebra.

quiz.say: If a predator attacks a group of zebras, the stripes might make it hard to focus on one animal. This is an example of:
quiz.why: The pattern breaks up the animal's outline, making it hard to see where one zebra ends and another begins.

wrong.0: This refers to keeping body temperature stable, not confusing sight.
wrong.1: Blending usually means matching the background, not creating a pattern.
wrong.3: Warning colors are usually bright and meant to say 'I am dangerous'.

quiz.say: If the stripes help the zebra stay cool, this is an example of:
quiz.why: This means the animal is controlling its body temperature using its coat pattern.

wrong.1: This describes confusing predators, which is a different function.
wrong.2: Mimicry means looking like something else entirely.
wrong.3: A warning display is usually a clear signal, not a pattern.

quiz.say: If the stripes confuse predators, this is best described as:
quiz.why: The pattern creates a flashing or confusing visual effect when the zebra moves.

wrong.1: Background matching means looking like the grass or dirt.
wrong.2: Heat absorption is about taking in warmth, not confusing sight.
wrong.3: A clear signal is something obvious, not something confusing.
